subject: GreenBank: ISO/FedRAMP pre-assessment — scope & exception scan request
messages:
From: Jason Lewis <jason.lewis@greenbank.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: security@greenbank.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: ISO/FedRAMP pre-assessment — initial ask

David,

Thanks again for the quick sync earlier. As we prepare GreenBank's pre-assessment packet I want to confirm a few things we need from Redwood to scope the FedRAMP readiness check and the ISO 27001 gap review. Can you confirm the following by EOD next week?

1) Current ISO 27001 scope document (system boundaries + excluded components) — we need the latest matrix so we can align our auditor checklist.
2) High-level network diagram showing segments that handle regulated customer workloads (preferably PNG/PDF).
3) A list of control exceptions and compensating controls historically tracked for SOC 2 /SIG requests — if you have a short export that shows the exception owner and mitigation status that would be ideal.
4) Any known data residency or cross-border processing flags for EU customers that would affect FedRAMP scoping.

Also, we typically run an "exceptions scan" to identify items that might create evidence sampling friction (e.g., ephemeral logs, short retention settings). Do you have a point person who can run a quick inventory with our intake form?

Attaching our intake template in case it's helpful — happy to take what you have and map it to our auditors' needs.

Thanks,
Jason
Director, IT Compliance
GreenBank Financial

Attachment: intake_template_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Jason Lewis <jason.lewis@greenbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ISO/FedRAMP pre-assessment — initial ask

Jason — thanks, and great list. We can get most of this over the next week. Quick answers up front:

• ISO scope matrix: we'll attach the current working copy (iso_scope_matrix.xlsx). It defines the service boundary for Redwood Inference hosted runtime and separates Dedicated/Private deployment options.
• Network diagram: attaching a simplified diagram for the regulated path (network_diagram.png).
• Control exceptions: we have a compact export of active exceptions and mitigations; I'll add that to the pack (exceptions_export_v2.csv) and include a brief readme on owners.
• Data residency: per-customer routing is in place — we have flags for eu/us/apac that determine storage and processing regions. No cross-border processing for GreenBank's EU customers by default (we'll provide the config extract).

Action plan:
1) Marissa will run an exceptions scan against the SIG/CAL questions and produce a short map to your intake template by Tuesday.
2) Priyom will package the relevant logs/retention statements and the export of exception records.
3) I'll schedule a 30-min preflight call for Monday 6/14 to walk the auditors through the artifacts and confirm sampling windows.

Marissa / Priyom — assigning owners below. Jason, please confirm if the Monday slot works.

Thanks,
David
Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: iso_scope_matrix.xlsx, network_diagram.png

Subject: Re: ISO/FedRAMP pre-assessment — initial ask

Jason / David — quick technical notes from my side as I start the exceptions scan:

• Sampling windows: auditors will ask for 90/180/365-day windows depending on the control. For infrastructure logs we can supply 90-day continuous snapshots; for access reviews we keep rolling 12-month evidence in the console. If GreenBank has specific snapshot dates (e.g., contract effective date), send them and I'll prioritize.
• Ephemeral artifacts: some internal debug logs are retained for 7 days; those are excluded from ISO scope by design. I'll flag any controls that rely on those artifacts and propose compensating evidence.
• Third-party attestations: we have SOC 2 Type II for the hosted API; SIG/CAIQ answers are in draft — I'll attach the latest export (sig_caiaq_responses.pdf) and a short README that maps to your intake columns.

Questions:
1) For FedRAMP scoping, do you intend to include the Dedicated offering under the same assessment or run a separate boundary? That impacts control baselines.
2) Any expectation on evidence delivery format (CSV vs. PDF vs. shared Drive path)? We can do both but want to standardize to reduce audit back-and-forth.

I'll have the first-pass exceptions map and the sample list ready by EOD Monday.

Marissa
Sr. Compliance Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sig_caiaq_responses.pdf

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, security@greenbank.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: ISO/FedRAMP pre-assessment — initial ask

Thanks — Monday works for an initial 30-min call. A couple of follow-ups before the call:

• Boundary question: GreenBank would prefer the Dedicated offering to be covered under the same assessment if possible, since we anticipate moving regulated workloads to a Dedicated pool. Please note that could add the Dedicated management plane and provisioning APIs to the auditor scope.
• Evidence format: PDF exports and CSV manifests are fine; Doc links with view-only perms are preferred for large artifacts.

On data residency: attaching a short note from our privacy team — they want confirmation that any EU-customer key material is stored in-region and that backups do not replicate to US regions. If Redwood can provide the region routing config snapshot that would satisfy them.

I'll see you on Monday (please send calendar invite).

Jason
Director, IT Compliance
GreenBank Financial

Attachment: greenbank_privacy_note.pdf
